program.name: Boy Scouts Handbook 1911
program.description: The merit badges in the Boy Scouts Handbook, First Edition, 1911 (Boy Scouts of America), as printed then. Historical 1911 text, not a current or official Scouting America requirement. Many of these badges are obsolete or unsafe today. You do not need to do anything unsafe. Ask a trusted adult before you try any requirement, and skip what you cannot do safely. The wording, spelling and punctuation are kept as printed. This app is unofficial and is not recognized by Scouting America. Source: Project Gutenberg eBook #29558. The book is in the US public domain because of its age. If you live outside the US, check your local law.

requirements.text: Catch and name ten different species of fish: salmon or trout to be taken with flies; bass, pickerel, or pike to be caught with rod or reel, muskallonge to be caught by trolling.
Make a bait rod of three joints, straight and sound, 14 oz. or less in weight, 10 feet or less in length, to stand a strain of 1-1/2 lbs. at the tip, 13 lbs. at the grip.
Make a jointed fly-rod 8-10 feet long, 4-8 ozs. in weight, capable of casting a fly sixty feet.
Name and describe twenty-five different species of fish found in North American waters and give a complete list of the fishes ascertained by himself to inhabit a given body of water.
Give the history of the young of any species of wild fish from the time of hatching until the adult stage is reached.
